To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the density dependence of the spin (isopin) and the isospin terms of the Goghy effective interaction play a crucial role for a correct determination of the symmetry potential and symmetry energy at supraseaturation densities.

the density and isospin dependence in nuclear effective interactions play a crucial role for the determination of the single-nucleo potential at high densities, and that this is important for the simulation of nuclear reactions within the transport model approach.
the spin and density dependence of the nuclear effective interactions are important in the calculation of the symmetry potential at suprasatuation density and the corresponding symmetry energy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an accurate single particle potential and the corresponding symmetry energy for the simulation of nuclear reactions in transport models.
the development of a new method for the calculation of the single-nucleus potential and the symmetry potential in the nuclear matter.

the study of the nuclear symmetry energy at high density, which has been recognized as an essential ingredient in the understanding of the properties of neutron stars and the equation of state (EOS) for neutron-rich nuclear matter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the symmetry potential at suprasatuation density, as well as the symmetry energy at high density, are sensitive to the isospin and density dependence of the effective interactions, and the density dependence plays a crucial role.
the symmetry energy is a complex function of the density and isospin asymmetry, and that the symmetry energy depends strongly on the density and isoscaling parameters.
the isospin-dependent single-nucleon optical potential is a very important ingredient for the description of heavy ion reaction dynamics at intermediate and high energies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the improved single-nucleus potential is very important for transport model simulations, and the improved single-nuclear potential will be useful in future simulations of reactions induced by rare isotopes beams.

, by using a more accurate expression of the symmetry energy, the symmetry energy at high densities could be better determined, which would be useful to constrain the symmetry energy in the equation of state of neutron star matter.

the isospin and spin dependence of the in-medium many body force term of the effective interaction plays a crucial role for the symmetry energy and the single nucleon potential at suprasatuation densities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the symmetry potential and symmetry energy should be determined self-consistently from nuclear effective interactions.

the symmetry potential and symmetry energy at supranormal densities should be determined from microscopic calculations based on realistic nuclear effective interactions, and the isospin (and spin) dependence of the nuclear effective interaction should be taken into account in the many-body force term.
the isospin and density dependence of the nuclear effective interaction is very crucial to obtain the correct symmetry potential and the correct symmetry energy at supraseaturation density.
